title: The PC BIOS data area
covers: The BIOS data area cells in segment 0040h.

rows.text: Base I/O address of the first serial port, a word.
The BIOS stores the base I/O address of the port in this word.
The BIOS sets this word to zero if it finds no serial port at the addresses it checks at boot.
DOSBox-X keeps the word at physical address 0x400.
DOSBox-X also stores 10 in the serial port 1 timeout byte at 0x47C.
Base I/O address of the second serial port, a word.
The BIOS stores the base I/O address of the port in this word.
The BIOS sets this word to zero if it finds no more than one serial port at boot.
DOSBox-X keeps the word at physical address 0x402.
DOSBox-X also stores 10 in the serial port 2 timeout byte at 0x47D.
Base I/O address of the third serial port, a word.
The BIOS sets this word to zero if it finds no more than two serial ports at boot.
DOSBox-X keeps the word at physical address 0x404.
Base I/O address of the fourth serial port, a word.
The BIOS sets this word to zero if it finds no more than three serial ports at boot.
DOSBox-X keeps the word at physical address 0x406.
Base I/O address of the first parallel port, a word.
The BIOS stores a parallel port's base I/O address in this field.
The POST routine fills the fields in turn as it finds parallel ports.
All fields beyond the last parallel port found are set to zero.
The BIOS INT 17 handler uses these fields to address the parallel ports.
DOSBox-X keeps the word at physical address 0x408.
DOSBox-X also stores 10 in the parallel port 1 timeout byte at 0x478.
Base I/O address of the second parallel port, a word.
Zero if fewer than two parallel ports are installed.
DOSBox-X keeps the word at physical address 0x40a.
DOSBox-X also stores 10 in the parallel port 2 timeout byte at 0x479.
Base I/O address of the third parallel port, a word.
Zero if fewer than three parallel ports are installed.
DOSBox-X keeps the word at physical address 0x40c.
DOSBox-X also stores 10 in the parallel port 3 timeout byte at 0x47A.
Base I/O address of the fourth parallel port, a word, before the PS/2.
Zero if fewer than four parallel ports are installed.
DOSBox-X names the word 0x40e for older machines and 0x40e as the extended BIOS data segment.
DOSBox-X stores the base addresses of only three parallel ports; its function has no case for the fourth.
Installed hardware, a word.
Bits 15-14 hold the number of parallel devices; 00 or 11 sometimes means four ports.
Bit 13 an internal modem on the Convertible and PS/2-55LS, 12 a game port installed.
Bits 11-9 hold the number of serial devices; 000 or 111 sometimes means eight ports.
Bit 8 is reserved.
Bits 7-6 hold the number of floppy disk drives minus one.
Bits 5-4 hold the initial video mode: 00 EGA or VGA, 01 40x25 color, 10 80x25 color, 11 80x25 mono.
Bits 3-2 hold motherboard RAM: 16K, 32K, 48K or 64K on the PC, 64K to 256K on some XTs.
Bit 2 is reserved on pre-PS/2 machines except the PC; a pointing device is installed on the PS/2, some XT clones and newer BIOSes.
Bit 1 a math coprocessor installed; bit 0 floppy disk drives are installed or booted from floppy.
DOSBox-X always sets bits 7-6 to 01, reporting two floppy drives whatever is configured.
DOSBox-X keeps the word at 0x410 and maps its bits in the comment beside it.
Convertible: POST status, a byte.
AT: undocumented manufacturing test initialization flags; bit 0 starts manufacturing test mode, bits 1-7 unused.
MCA: manufacturing test flags; bit 0 selects the mode, other bits are POST flags or unused.
PS/2 Model 25: POST system flag; bit 0 optional memory failed and was remapped, bit 1 real-time clock installed.
DOSBox-X marks the byte at 0x412 reserved as a possible POST flag.
Base memory size in kilobytes, a word.
DOSBox-X names the word 0x413 BIOS_MEMORY_SIZE.
PC and XT: adapter memory size in kilobytes, a word.
AT: undocumented manufacturing test scratch pad, a byte.
Compaq Deskpro 386: previous scan code, a byte.
DOSBox-X names a word at 0x415 BIOS_TRUE_MEMORY_SIZE.
AT: undocumented manufacturing test scratch pad, a byte.
PS/2 Model 30: undocumented BIOS control flags, a byte.
Compaq Deskpro 386: keyclick volume, a byte from 00h to 7Fh.
DOSBox-X names a word at 0x415; the byte at 0x416 is its high half.
Keyboard status flags 1, a byte.
Bit 7 INSert active, 6 Caps Lock active, 5 Num Lock active, 4 Scroll Lock active.
Bit 3 either Alt pressed, 2 either Ctrl pressed, 1 Left Shift pressed, 0 Right Shift pressed.
DOSBox-X keeps the byte at 0x417 and defines the same eight bits.
Keyboard status flags 2, a byte.
Bit 7 INSert pressed, 6 Caps Lock pressed, 5 Num Lock pressed, 4 Scroll Lock pressed.
Bit 3 Pause state active, 2 Sys Req pressed, 1 Left Alt pressed, 0 Left Ctrl pressed.
DOSBox-X keeps the byte at 0x418 and defines the same eight bits.
Holds the current value of an Alt-nnn keypad sequence.
When Alt is released and this byte is non-zero, the character is placed in the keyboard buffer.
DOSBox-X keeps the workspace byte at 0x419.
Pointer to the next character in the keyboard buffer, a word.
DOSBox-X keeps the head pointer at 0x41a.
Pointer to the first free slot in the keyboard buffer, a word.
DOSBox-X keeps the tail pointer at 0x41c.
The default keyboard circular buffer, sixteen words.
DOSBox-X keeps the sixteen-word buffer at 0x41e.
Diskette recalibrate status, a byte.
Bit 7 a diskette hardware interrupt occurred, bits 6-4 reserved.
Bit 3 recalibrate diskette 3 and bit 2 diskette 2 on the PC and XT only, 1 diskette 1, 0 diskette 0.
DOSBox-X keeps the recalibration byte at 0x43e.
Diskette motor status, a byte.
Bit 7 the current operation is write or format rather than read or verify, bit 6 reserved.
Bits 5-4 the selected diskette drive; bit 3 motor on for diskette 3 and bit 2 diskette 2 on the PC and XT only; 1 diskette 1, 0 diskette 0.
DOSBox-X keeps the motor status byte at 0x43f.
Number of clock ticks until the diskette motor is turned off, a byte.
Typically the INT 08 handler decrements this byte on every tick and turns the motor off when the result is zero.
DOSBox-X's INT 08 handler decrements the byte each tick and stops the motors at zero, but wraps it below zero on a machine that is not EGA or VGA.
DOSBox-X keeps the timeout count at 0x440.
Diskette last operation status, a byte.
Bits 7 drive not ready, 6 seek error, 5 general controller failure, 4-0 the error reason.
Error reason 00h none, 01h invalid request, 02h address mark not found, 03h write protect, 04h sector not found.
Error reason 06h diskette change, 08h DMA overrun, 09h DMA across a 64K boundary, 0Ch unknown media, 10h CRC error.
This byte also takes 30h no media sense, 31h no media, 32h no media type support and AAh not ready, which differ from the bitfield above.
DOSBox-X names the status byte at 0x441.
The seven bytes at 42h hold floppy or hard disk status and command bytes.
XT: 42h is the command byte to the hard disk controller; AT: the write precompensation cylinder number divided by four.
43h in the XT holds the drive in bit 5 and the head in bits 3-0; in the AT it is the sector count.
44h in the XT holds the high track bits in 7-6 and the start sector minus one in 5-0; in the AT the starting sector.
45h is the low byte of the track number.
46h in the XT is the sector count; in the AT the high bits of the track number.
47h in the XT is the control byte from the drive parameters; in the AT bit 7 ECC, 6 unknown, 5 512-byte sectors, 4 drive and 3-0 head.
48h in the XT is the INT 13h subfunction number; in the AT the command byte to the hard disk controller.
The same byte at 42h also holds the diskette controller's status register 0.
Bits 7-6 hold the interrupt code: 00 normal, 01 abnormal during execution, 10 invalid command, 11 abnormal termination or diskette change.
Bit 5 requested seek complete, 4 drive fault, 3 drive not ready, 2 head state at interrupt, 1-0 the selected drive.
DOSBox-X names the seven-byte block at 0x442 for status and command bytes.
Diskette controller status register 1, a byte.
Bit 7 attempted access beyond the last cylinder, 6 unused, 5 CRC error on read, 4 DMA overrun.
Bit 3 unused, 2 data error, 1 disk write protected, 0 missing address mark.
DOSBox-X names 0x443 as the second byte of the status block at 0x442.
Diskette controller status register 2, a byte.
Bit 7 unused, 6 found a deleted data address mark, 5 CRC error in the data field, 4 wrong cylinder number read.
Bit 3 verify equal, 2 no sector matches the verify condition, 1 bad cylinder, 0 unable to find address mark.
DOSBox-X names 0x444 as the third byte of the status block at 0x442.
Current video mode, a byte.
DOSBox-X names the mode byte at 0x449.
Number of columns on the screen, a word.
DOSBox-X names the column count at 0x44a.
Size of the page in the regeneration buffer, in bytes, a word.
DOSBox-X names the page size at 0x44c.
Start address of the current page in the regeneration buffer, a word.
DOSBox-X names the page start at 0x44e.
Video cursor positions, eight words.
Contains the row and column position for the cursors on each of eight video pages.
DOSBox-X keeps an eight-entry cursor position array at 0x450.
Cursor type, a big-endian word holding the cursor start scan line and end scan line.
DOSBox-X names the word at 0x460 and its bytes as the cursor's last and first line.
Current video page number, a byte.
DOSBox-X keeps the current screen page at 0x462.
CRT controller base I/O port address, a word.
Normally 3B4h for mono and 3D4h for color video boards.
DOSBox-X names the CRT controller base port at 0x463.
Current mode select register, a byte.
Holds the last value written to I/O port 3B8h or 3D8h.
Bits 7-6 unused, 5 attribute bit 7 controls blinking instead of background, 4 mode 6 graphics in monochrome, 3 video signal enabled.
Bit 2 monochrome, 1 graphics, 0 80x25 text.
DOSBox-X names the VDU control byte at 0x465.
Current setting of the CGA palette register, a byte.
Holds the last value written to I/O port 3D9h.
Bits 7-6 unused, 5 palette 0 or 1, 4 intense background colors in text mode, 3 intense border color in 40x25 or background color in mode 5.
Bit 2 red, 1 green, 0 blue.
DOSBox-X names the VDU color register at 0x466.
PC only: cassette time count, a word.
Reset restart address: where to resume after a CPU reset, or a jump to F000h:FFF0h, when certain magic values are stored at 0040h:0072h or in CMOS location 0Fh.
DOSBox-X names a far pointer at 0x467 that it jumps to after a specific 286 reset.
PC only: cassette CRC register, a word.
DOSBox-X gives 0x467 a 32-bit post-reset vector, whose high word covers 0x469.
PC only: last value read from cassette, a byte.
XT and later: a bitmask of the IRQs that occurred while their vector pointed at the default BIOS handler; IRQ0-7 in bits 0-7, IRQ8-15 in bit 2 on AT.
DOSBox-X names the byte at 0x46b; its default IRQ handler reads master_isr from the master PIC and stores it there.
Timer ticks since midnight, a dword.
Updated approximately every 55 milliseconds by the BIOS INT 08 handler.
DOSBox-X keeps a 32-bit timer tick count at 0x46c.
Timer overflow, a byte: non-zero if the timer has counted past midnight since the last INT 1A/AH=00h call.
The original IBM BIOS, and most other BIOSes, sets this byte to 01h at midnight; a few increment it each time midnight is passed.
DOSBox-X names the midnight rollover byte at 0x470.
Ctrl-Break flag, a byte.
Bit 7 is set when Ctrl-Break has been pressed.
DOSBox-X names the Ctrl-Break flag at 0x471.
POST reset flag, a word.
Specifies the action the BIOS should take at the beginning of the power-on self-test when the machine is reset.
Values: 0000h cold boot, 0064h Burn-in mode, 1234h bypass the memory test (warm boot).
4321h preserve memory (PS/2 except Mod 25,30), 5678h system suspended, 9ABCh manufacturing test, ABCDh POST loop; the last three are conventional.
DOSBox-X names the reset flag word at 0x472.
Fixed disk last operation status, a byte (except ESDI drives).
Values: 00h no error, 01h invalid function request, 02h address mark not found, 03h write protect error.
04h sector not found, 05h reset failed, 06h diskette removed, 07h drive parameter activity failed, 08h DMA overrun, 09h DMA data boundary error.
0Ah bad sector flag detected, 0Bh bad track detected, 0Ch requested diskette media type not found or, on PS/2 or extended BIOS only, unsupported track.
0Dh invalid number of sectors for Format, 0Eh control data address mark detected, 0Fh DMA arbitration level out of range, 10h uncorrectable ECC or CRC error.
11h ECC corrected data error, 20h general controller failed, 40h seek failed, 80h time out.
AAh drive not ready, B0h volume not locked, B1h volume locked, B2h volume not removable, B3h volume in use, B4h lock count exceeded (INT 13 extensions).
B5h valid eject request failed (INT 13 extensions), BBh undefined error, CCh write fault on the selected drive, E0h status error or the error register is zero, FFh sense failed.
DOSBox-X names the fixed disk status byte at 0x474.
Number of fixed disk drives, a byte.
DOSBox-X names the hard disk count at 0x475.
Fixed disk control byte, a byte; IBM documented only for XT.
Loaded from the disk parameter table control byte (offset 8) during various hard disk operations.
XT: hard disk controller's I/O address (Western Digital).
DOSBox-X names the XT-only fixed disk control byte at 0x476.
Fixed disk I/O port offset, a byte; IBM documented only for XT.
DOSBox-X names the XT-only fixed disk I/O port offset at 0x477.
Parallel device 1 time-out counter, a byte.
DOSBox-X names the LPT1 time-out byte at 0x478.
Parallel device 2 time-out counter, a byte.
DOSBox-X names the LPT2 time-out byte at 0x479.
Parallel device 3 time-out counter, a byte.
DOSBox-X names the LPT3 time-out byte at 0x47a.
Parallel device 4 time-out counter, a byte (pre-PS, PS models 25,30).
PS/2 and newer: INT 4Bh flags, a byte.
Bits 7-6 reserved, 5 Virtual DMA Spec supported, 4 reserved, 3 INT 4Bh intercepted and must be chained, 2 reserved, 1 Generic SCSI CBIOS services available, 0 reserved.
DOSBox-X names a time-out byte at 0x47b and bit 5 of it as Virtual DMA support.
Serial device 1 time-out counter, a byte.
DOSBox-X names the COM1 time-out byte at 0x47c.
Serial device 2 time-out counter, a byte.
DOSBox-X names the COM2 time-out byte at 0x47d.
Serial device 3 time-out counter, a byte.
DOSBox-X names the COM3 time-out byte at 0x47e.
Serial device 4 time-out counter, a byte.
DOSBox-X names the COM4 time-out byte at 0x47f.
Offset from segment 40h of the keyboard buffer start, a word; normally 1Eh.
DOSBox-X names the keyboard buffer start offset at 0x480.
Offset from segment 40h one past the keyboard buffer end, a word; normally 3Eh.
DOSBox-X names the keyboard buffer end offset at 0x482.
EGA/MCGA/VGA: rows on screen minus one, a byte.
DOSBox-X names the row count minus one at 0x484.
EGA/MCGA/VGA: character height in scan lines, a word.
DOSBox-X names the character height at 0x485.
EGA/VGA video control, a byte; MCGA: 00h.
Bit 7: do not clear RAM on mode set; 6-5 RAM on adapter = (this field + 1) * 64K; 4 reserved; 3 EGA/VGA video system inactive.
Bit 2 wait for display enable, 1 mono monitor, 0 alphanumeric cursor emulation disabled; when enabled, text cursor sizes looking like CGA ones are translated to EGA/VGA ones.
DOSBox-X names the EGA/VGA control byte at 0x487.
EGA/VGA switches, a byte; on MCGA the byte is reserved.
Bits 7-4 hold the power-on state of feature connector bits 3-0; bits 3-0 are configuration switches 4-1, 0 on and 1 off.
When bit 4 of 0040h:0089h is clear, VGA emulates a 350-line EGA if this byte is x3h or x9h, else a 200-line CGA in 400-line double scan.
VGA resets this byte to x9h after the mode set.
Values 00h-0Bh pair a primary and a secondary display among MDA, CGA, EGA with old color display, EGA+ECD in normal or enhanced mode, and EGA mono.
DOSBox-X names the byte at 0x488 as the EGA/VGA switches.
DOSBox-X also names 0x488 as the PCjr second keyboard flag byte, with eight flag bits.
Video mode-set option control, a byte.
Bits 7 and 4, requested scan lines: 00 350-line mode, 01 400-line at the next mode set, 10 200-line mode, 11 reserved.
Apparently the VGA BIOS mode set disregards bit 7 and uses 40h:88h to choose 200 or 350 lines when bit 4 is zero.
Presumably bit 7 is a convenience for other purposes; it is reset to zero after the mode set.
Bit 6 display switching enabled; bit 5 reserved.
Bit 4 set: use 400-line mode at the next mode set; clear: VGA emulates EGA, MCGA emulates CGA with a digital monitor, 200 lines and 8x8 text.
This bit is set by the video mode set on VGA and unchanged on MCGA.
Bit 3 default palette loading disabled at the mode set, 2 mono display, 1 gray scale summing enabled.
Bit 0 is 1 if VGA is active and 0 if not; on MCGA it is reserved and zero.
DOSBox-X names the byte at 0x489 as the MCGA/VGA control byte.
Index into the display combination code table, a byte.
DOSBox-X names the byte at 0x48A as the MCGA/VGA display combination code byte.
On the PC, PCjr, PC/XT of 11/8/82 and Convertible, 11 bytes from 008Bh are reserved.
Diskette media control, a byte.
Bits 7-6 last data rate set by the controller: 00 500, 01 300, 10 250 kbps, 11 1 Mbps.
Bits 5-4 last drive step rate selected: 00 0Ch, 01 0Dh, 10 0Eh, 11 0Ah.
Bits 3-2 the data rate at the start of the operation; bits 1-0 reserved.
The EHD BIOS sets this byte to 01h and never reads it back.
DOSBox-X names the byte at 0x48B as the floppy media control byte.
Fixed disk controller status, a byte, on machines other than the XT.
DOSBox-X names the byte at 0x48C as the fixed disk controller status byte.
Fixed disk controller error status, a byte, on machines other than the XT.
DOSBox-X names the byte at 0x48D as the fixed disk controller error byte.
Fixed disk interrupt control, a byte, on machines other than the XT.
Cleared to 00h at the start of a disk operation and set to FFh by the IRQ14 handler when the controller completes the command.
DOSBox-X names the byte at 0x48E as the fixed disk interrupt control byte.
Diskette controller information, a byte, on machines other than the XT.
Bit 7 reserved; 6 set if drive 1 is determined, 5 if drive 1 is multi-rate, valid when determined, 4 if drive 1 supports 80 tracks.
Bit 3 reserved; 2 set if drive 0 is determined, 1 if drive 0 is multi-rate, valid when determined, 0 if drive 0 supports 80 tracks.
The EHD BIOS sets this byte to 01h and never alters it again.
DOSBox-X names the byte at 0x48F as the diskette controller information byte.
Media state of diskette drive 0, a byte.
Bits 7-6 data rate: 00 500, 01 300, 10 250 kbps, 11 1 Mbps.
Bit 5 double stepping required (e.g. 360kB in 1.2MB), 4 media type established, 3 drive supports 4MB media.
Bits 2-0 on exit from the BIOS: 000 trying 360kB in 360kB, 001 trying 360kB in 1.2MB, 010 trying 1.2MB in 1.2MB.
011 360kB in 360kB established, 100 360kB in 1.2MB established, 101 1.2MB in 1.2MB established, 110 reserved, 111 other formats.
DOSBox-X names the byte at 0x490 as the media state byte of floppy drive 0.
Media state of diskette drive 1, a byte, with the same bitfields as drive 0 at 0040h:0090h.
DOSBox-X names the byte at 0x491 as the media state byte of floppy drive 1.
Media state of diskette drive 0 at the start of an operation, a byte; the list says officially Drive 2 media state.
Bits 7-3 as in 0040h:0090h; 2 multiple data rate capability determined, 1 multiple data rate capability.
Bit 0 is 1 if the drive has 80 tracks and 0 if it has 40.
DOSBox-X names the byte at 0x492 as the media state of floppy drive 0 at the start of an operation.
Media state of diskette drive 1 at the start of an operation, a byte; officially Drive 3 media state.
Bits 7-3 see #M0030; 2 multiple data rate capability determined, 1 multiple data rate capability, 0 =1 if 80 tracks.
DOSBox-X names the byte at 0x493 as the media state of floppy drive 1 at the start of an operation.
Current track number of diskette drive 0, a byte.
DOSBox-X names the byte at 0x494 as the current track byte of floppy drive 0.
DOSBox-X writes the cylinder to 0x494 plus the drive number, so one store covers this byte and drive 1's.
Current track number of diskette drive 1, a byte.
DOSBox-X names the byte at 0x495 as the current track byte of floppy drive 1.
Keyboard status byte 1, a byte.
Bit 7 read-ID in progress, 6 last code read was first of two ID codes, 5 force Num Lock if read-ID and enhanced keyboard, 4 enhanced keyboard installed.
Bit 3 Right Alt pressed, 2 Right Ctrl pressed, 1 last code read was E0h, 0 last code read was E1h.
DOSBox-X names the byte at 0x496 and defines the same eight bits.
Keyboard status byte 2, a byte.
Bit 7 keyboard transmit error, 6 LED update in progress, 5 RESEND received, 4 ACK received, 3 reserved and must be zero.
Bit 2 Caps Lock LED, 1 Num Lock LED, 0 Scroll Lock LED.
DOSBox-X names the byte at 0x497 as the keyboard LED byte.
Pointer to the user wait-complete flag, a dword, for INT 15/AX=8300h.
DOSBox-X names the far pointer at 0x498.
With INT 15/AH=86h DOSBox-X points the dword at a temporary flag byte at 0x4A1.
User wait count in microseconds, a dword.
DOSBox-X names the wait count at 0x49C.
DOSBox-X subtracts 997 from the count on each timer interrupt and sets it to zero below that.
HP 100LX/200LX video zoom mode, a byte.
02h 80x25 mono, 03h 80x25 color, 80h 64x18 mono, 81h 64x18 color, 82h 40x25 mono, 83h 40x25 color.
84h 40x16 mono, 85h 40x16 color.
DOSBox-X addresses the BIOS data area at its linear base, offset by the byte address minus 0x400.
Timer2 wait active flag, a byte.
Bit 7 wait time elapsed; bits 6-1 reserved; bit 0 INT 15/AH=86h has occurred.
DOSBox-X names the wait active flag at 0x4A0.
DOSBox-X clears the active flag when the count reaches zero.
Bit 5 is set if the LAN Support Program interrupt arbitrator is present (device DXMA0MOD.SYS), a byte.
DOSBox-X names seven LAN bytes from 0x4A1.
DOSBox-X also names 0x4A1 as the temporary wait flag it points the wait pointer at.
Six bytes from 00A2h are reserved for network adapters.
DOSBox-X reserves seven bytes from 0x4A1 as a LAN block.
On the PS/2 Model 30, a saved fixed disk interrupt vector, a dword.
DOSBox-X addresses the BIOS data area at its linear base, offset by the byte address minus 0x400.
Pointer to the video save pointer table, a dword.
Save Pointer Table: 00h dword pointer to the Video Parameter Table, 04h dword Parameter Dynamic Save Area, else 0 (EGA/VGA only).
08h dword Alphanumeric Character Set Override, else 0, 0Ch dword Graphics Character Set Override, else 0.
10h dword Secondary Save Pointer Table (VGA only, must be valid), 14h and 18h dwords reserved zero.
The table is initially in ROM; copy it to RAM to alter it, then update 0040h:00A8h.
Secondary Video Save Pointer Table (VGA): 00h word its length in bytes including the word (1Ah), 02h dword Display Combination Code Table, must be valid.
06h dword second Alphanumeric Character Set Override, 0Ah dword User Palette Profile Table, 0Eh, 12h and 16h reserved zero.
This table too is initially in ROM; copy it to RAM to alter it, then alter the Save Pointer Table.
Display Combination Code Table: 00h number of entries at offset 04h, 01h version number, 02h maximum display type code, 03h reserved.
04h: 2N bytes, each pair a valid display combination, one display type per byte.
Display type 00h no display, 01h MDA mono, 02h CGA color, 03h reserved, 04h EGA color, 05h EGA mono, 06h Professional Graphics Controller.
07h VGA mono, 08h VGA color, 09h reserved, 0Ah MCGA digital color, 0Bh MCGA analog mono, 0Ch MCGA analog color, FFh unrecognized video system.
Video Parameter Table (EGA, VGA): 00h-03h modes 00h-03h in 200-line CGA emulation, 04h-0Eh modes 04h-0Eh, 0Fh-10h modes 0Fh-10h with only 64kB.
11h-12h modes 0Fh-10h with more than 64kB, 13h-16h modes 00h-03h in 350-line mode, 17h-19h VGA 400-line modes, 1Ah-1Ch VGA modes 11h-13h.
An array of 23 EGA or 29 VGA elements of 64 bytes, in that order.
Video Parameter Table element: 00h columns on screen, 01h rows on screen minus one, 02h character height in scan lines, 03h word video buffer size.
05h four bytes for Sequencer Registers 1-4, 09h Miscellaneous Output Register, 0Ah 25 bytes CRTC registers 00h-18h.
23h 20 bytes Attribute Controller registers 00h-13h, 37h nine bytes Graphics Controller registers 00h-08h.
The MCGA Video Parameter Table is guesswork from inspection: 16 triplets of RGB DAC data for 16 colors, then 11 elements of 32 bytes.
The elements cover modes 00h-06h and 13h, each in 200-line mode for digital and 400-line mode for analog displays; mode 11h is listed without either.
MCGA element: 00h columns, 01h rows minus one, 02h character height, 03h word video buffer size.
05h word marked ???, always zero, 07h 21 bytes video data registers 00h-14h to port 3D5h indexed by 3D4h, 1Ch PEL mask to port 3C6h.
1Dh CGA mode control to port 3D8h, 1Eh CGA border control to port 3D9h, 1Fh extended mode control to port 3DDh.
Video Parameter Dynamic Save Area: 00h 16 bytes last data written to Attribute Controller palette registers 0-15, 10h last data to the overscan register.
11h-FFh reserved; the area exists because the EGA registers were write-only.
When a mode set overrides the defaults from the User Palette Profile Table, the save area takes the default values, not the profile ones.
Alphanumeric Character Set Override: 00h length of each character in bytes, 01h character generator RAM bank to load (0 normal), 02h number of characters (normally 256).
04h code of the first character (normally 0), 06h dword pointer to the font table, 0Ah displayable rows (FFh uses the maximum calculated).
0Bh an array of mode values the font pertains to, ended by FFh.
Second Alphanumeric Character Set Override: 00h byte length of each character, 01h character generator RAM bank (normally non-zero), 02h reserved.
03h dword pointer to the font table, 07h an array of mode values ended by FFh.
Authorities differ: some say this table is as the first override, but IBM says it is as shown.
Graphics Character Set Override: 00h number of displayable rows, 01h word length of each character, 03h dword pointer to the font table.
07h an array of mode values ended by FFh.
User Palette Profile Table (VGA): 00h underlining 01h enabled in all alphanumeric modes, 00h monochrome ones only, FFh disabled in all.
01h reserved, 02h word reserved, 04h number (0-17) of Attribute Controller registers, 06h index (0-16) of the first.
08h dword pointer to the byte array of Attribute Controller registers to override.
0Ch number (0-256) of video DAC color registers, 0Eh index (0-255) of the first.
10h dword pointer to the table of video DAC color registers, whose form the list marks as doubtful.
14h an array of mode values the profile pertains to, ended by FFh.
DOSBox-X names the far pointer at 0x4A8.
Four bytes, reserved.
DOSBox-X addresses the BIOS data area at its linear base, offset by the byte address minus 0x400.
Phoenix 386 BIOS 1.10 10a: number of times a tight software delay loop should be executed to generate the BIOS's internal sub-55ms delays, a byte.
